objectives: Identify and remediate short /i/ weaknesses revealed by the diagnostic.
Use minimal contrasts to repair /i/ versus /a/ confusion.
Strengthen decoding, encoding, comprehension or fluency according to the observed gap.
Reassess the repaired skill and make an advance-or-reteach decision.
concepts: Remediation should target the diagnosed component rather than reteach everything.
Minimal contrasts make vowel differences explicit.
Progression should depend on evidence, not completion speed.

definitions.definition: Instruction focused on a specific diagnosed learning gap.
A follow-up check using new items to determine whether the target skill has improved.
An evidence-based decision to advance or provide further reteaching.

workedExamples: sit/sat → hear the middle vowel → map i/a → spell and read both.
pin/pan → compare middle phonemes → decode again → spell the target word.
Accurate but slow reading → repeated accurate reading before increasing speed.
commonMistakes: Reteaching every skill instead of the diagnosed gap.
Using identical assessment items as the only evidence.
Advancing because the learner finished quickly.
Increasing speed before accuracy is secure.
keyTakeaways: Advance only when evidence supports it.
revisionPoints: Diagnose → target → practise → reassess → advance or reteach.

basic: Contrast short /i/ and /a/ in minimal pairs.
conceptual: Identify the component skill behind an error.
application: Repair decoding and spelling errors using sound-to-letter mapping.
higherOrderThinking: Select the correct next instructional decision from assessment evidence.
mixedReview: Combine vowel contrast, decoding, spelling, comprehension and fluency repair.

formulaOrFactBank: Mastery decision = evidence against defined target
mistakeBasedRevision: i/a confusion → auditory contrast + grapheme mapping.
slow accurate reading → repeated accurate rereading.
weakTopicRevision: Repeat only the weak component, then use fresh reassessment items.

outcomes: Learner improves the diagnosed short /i/ component with targeted practice.
Learner distinguishes short /i/ from /a/ in taught contrasts with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner applies corrected sound-spelling mapping to new CVC items.
Teacher can make an evidence-based advance-or-reteach decision.
